newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan condemns Jerusalem bombing as "act of terror".
newsitem.headline: Annan condemns Jerusalem bombing as "act of terror".

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Wednesday he was shocked and horrified by the bombing of a market in West Jerusalem and unreservedly condemned "this act of terror."

"This is a crucial time in the quest for peace in the Middle East. I appeal to all concerned to reject violence and pursue their aims through dialogue, at the negotiating table," he said in a statement.
Annan was reacting to an attack by two Arab suicide bombers on Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market that killed 13 people and wounded more than 150.
"I am shocked and horrified by the carnage in Jerusalem today," the U.N. chief said.

"I express my heartfelt condolences to the government and people of Israel, and especially to the families of the victims. And I condemn this act of terror unreservedly, as I condemn terrorism from whatever quarter. Violence of this kind can never advance the cause of peace."
Earlier, speaking to Cable News Network (CNN), Annan called the bombing "abominable and unfortunate, particularly at a time when all efforts are being made to get the peace talks back on track."
"And I appeal to all involved to avoid the use of bombs and violence and really get back to the negotiating table," he added.

He recalled telling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a telephone conversation on Monday he was encouraged that he had suspended construction of a controversial housing project in an Arab neighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
"And so I am disappointed that at a crucial time when we were just on the verge of getting the talks back on track that this should happen," Annan told CNN.
